record_verbatim.objective: Confirm that no byte on the serial receive line reaches the application layer without passing a length check and an integrity check, that a structurally valid frame with a modified payload is rejected, that neither 0x13 nor 0x11 can change the transmit-enabled state outside an authenticated frame, and that a receive overflow is diagnosable.

oracle_detail.known_limitation_in_the_requirement: As with the CAN measure, the 'genuine frames rejected: 0' criterion was unsatisfiable for a practical integrity value and has been revised under finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. It now bounds the rate at 1 per 10^6 genuine frames, demonstrated as 0 rejections over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6, and requires the integrity value to be at least 22 bits. The bounds it does not carry are the same as the CAN measure's: the bound holds only at the population stated, and it says nothing about the secrecy of the key, about resynchronisation after a desynchronising error, or about whether an authenticated peer is entitled to command what it commands.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: The oracle says nothing about the strength of the integrity value, about re-synchronisation after a desynchronising error, or about whether an authenticated peer is entitled to command what it commands. It also does not cover the availability consequence: a receiver that discards everything malformed but never resynchronises passes every expected outcome here and is unusable.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no serial traffic was sent or captured. It is not an analytical model: there is no model of the receiver's parser. It is not a synthetic assumption: admissibility is decidable by the receiver by construction.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the framing rule's own definition, read from the requirement. A frame is admissible only when its declared length equals the received byte count and its integrity value verifies; both are decidable by the receiver alone, so a byte outside such a frame has no admissible interpretation and must be discarded. The control-byte clause follows from the same definition: 0x13 and 0x11 are payload byte values, and a value that is privileged only inside an authenticated frame cannot be reached outside one. The expected outcomes - zero bytes passing, zero transitions - are consequences of the rule, not observations of an implementation.

preconditions: The serial link under test is the link the item uses for its external service interface.
The item is otherwise nominal and no genuine peer is mid-transfer.
The receive queue depth is configured and known.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run on any change to the framing format, the integrity primitive, the key, the queue depth or the parser's resynchronisation behaviour. Any change that makes a byte actionable outside a verified frame must fail this measure.

revision_history.description: Security verification measure authored because FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 had no verifies or validates link in either direction (findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12) and contributed five of the validator's standing medium findings. The measure states its oracle basis explicitly and says which kind of oracle it is.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: Regenerated as a dependent of finding FB2-REV-FND-000028 after FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 revised its genuine-frame false-rejection criterion. The expected outcome genuine_frames_rejected no longer records the requirement's absolute 0; it records the population the rate bound is demonstrated over (>= 3 x 10^6 genuine frames in 24 h) and the pass condition derived from it (0 rejections observed over that population, i.e. a one-sided 95 percent upper confidence bound of 1 x 10^-6 by the rule of three), plus the observed genuine-frame population itself so that the bound can be recomputed by a reviewer rather than taken on trust. A new expected outcome records the integrity value width the requirement now mandates (>= 22 bits). The oracle_detail's known_limitation_in_the_requirement no longer states that the criterion is unachievable, because it is no longer unachievable; it now states what the revised criterion does and does not bound, and names the residual risks that a pass on this measure would NOT cover. Step 4's expected result was restated from 'Zero genuine frames rejected' to the population-plus-bound form for the same reason. Every other expected outcome - the zeros for injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, short frames accepted - is UNCHANGED: those are decidable by the check existing and were deliberately not relaxed. The measure remains planned and unexecuted; no execution evidence is claimed by this revision and human_approval_status remains pending.

record_verbatim.security_verification_note: This measure verifies the requirement as written against the item's observable behaviour. It does not establish that the threat it addresses is exploitable, and it is not a penetration test: no exploit was developed, no advisory was checked and no CVSS score was assigned to any finding.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
